parallel.requirements: The run recognized the need for pure ESM .mjs files in /output, manual --a/--b parsing, no npm dependencies, and character-level stdout compatibility.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent did early probing, then delegated the complete implementation and verification path to one coder child rather than splitting independent subscopes.
parallel.implementation: The child wrote jsonvalues, pointer, engine, keywords, drafts, argparse, pyjson, and test13 modules and iterated against executable probes.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The child wrote directly into /output; artifact validation later copied test13.mjs and the lib modules, so delivery existed despite no normal child handoff.
parallel.verification: The child reached PASS=316 FAIL=0 on an initial differential harness, then launched a larger extended sweep that was interrupted before a result.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The child never returned a completed result to the parent, extended verification remained unfinished, and the official evaluator still failed every testcase.

serial.requirements: The serial main actor recognized the same ESM, no-dependency, CLI, validator selection, JSON parsing, output, and black-box probing requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The serial run kept all ownership in the main actor, combining probing, implementation, integration, and verification without delegation.
serial.implementation: The main actor wrote json_parse, pytypes, resolver, keywords, drafts, validators, cli, and test13 modules and fixed mismatches from local harnesses.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial artifact contained the entry file, library modules, and local comparison scripts directly in /output with no merge from child agents.
serial.verification: The main actor passed a 151-case deterministic harness and a 74-case second battery, then generated 1250 fuzz cases and began comparing them.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The fuzz comparison result was not received before interruption, and the official evaluator still failed every testcase.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the ESM, .mjs, manual CLI, zero-dependency, black-box probing, and output-alignment requirements and passed them into the child prompt.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial received the same prompt and recognized the same implementation and acceptance obligations in its own initial reasoning and probes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement understanding was broadly similar; the difference was that parallel transferred requirements to a child while serial retained them locally.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used swarm mode and delegated the entire build and verification deliverable to one child after parent-side exploration.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all work in the main actor and protocol validation records no delegation or subagents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced a child lifecycle and parent-child join dependency; serial had no cross-agent ownership boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent transferred a detailed implementation brief with behavior notes, draft mappings, CLI requirements, and a suggested module layout to the child.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial accumulated the same task knowledge in one context and wrote modules directly without a handoff contract between agents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel context boundary was rich rather than missing, but it still created a child result dependency that serial avoided.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child wrote a modular validator implementation with json value utilities, pointer resolution, engine, keyword handlers, draft config, CLI parsing, and entrypoint.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The main actor wrote a separate modular implementation with parser, type helpers, resolver, keyword handlers, draft definitions, validator core, CLI, and entrypoint.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both produced broad JSON Schema implementations, but the file/module designs differed and neither passed the official evaluator.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child was active in an extended differential sweep when cancellation occurred, and the parent received `status: failed` rather than a completed child result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result to retrieve; it waited on its own background fuzz task and was interrupted locally.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's unfinished work crossed a parent-child lifecycle boundary, while serial's unfinished work was a local wait on a background command.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child wrote directly to /output and artifact validation copied test13.mjs plus seven library modules; no competing writer is evidenced.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The main actor wrote directly to /output and artifact validation copied test13.mjs, libraries, and comparison scripts; no shared writer is evidenced.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both delivered artifacts from direct /output writes, but parallel delivery depended on child side effects while serial delivery came from the main actor.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child passed a 316-case local differential harness but was interrupted before the larger extended sweep returned.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial passed 151-case and 74-case local batteries, generated 1250 fuzz cases, and was interrupted while waiting for fuzz comparison output.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost verification at a child boundary; serial completed two local batteries before a local fuzz wait remained unfinished.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel process timed out after using one subagent, and both child and parent turns were cancelled around the extended sweep.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial process also timed out, but it had no subagent and cancellation occurred during a local TaskOutput wait.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both ran out of budget, but only parallel converted that closure into a stopped child and failed parent-child handoff.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed status.json evaluations make this a both_fail pair: each mode scored 0/166 and solution_passed false. The parallel run suffered a concrete coordination loss when its implementation child was cancelled before returning a completed handoff, whereas the serial run avoided child coordination and completed two local differential batteries before its own fuzz wait was interrupted. That difference explains process quality and closure differences, but not a discordant official result because neither artifact passed the official evaluator.
parallel_contributors: The parent delegated the full implementation and verification path to a child and then received only a failed child result after cancellation.
The child wrote an artifact and reached one local green harness, but extended verification was interrupted before a completed handoff.
serial_contributors: The serial main actor kept implementation and verification in one context and completed two deterministic local harnesses.
The serial run still timed out while waiting on a background fuzz comparison and also failed the official evaluator.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The two runs produced different module layouts and likely different validator behavior beyond their local harnesses.
Both relied on self-generated differential tests rather than evidence aligned to the official 166-case evaluator.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause

candidates.reason: The parent assigned implementation to agent-0, and that child wrote the library modules and entrypoint.
There were not separately owned component implementations needing a missing cross-agent integrator; the single child owned the implementation.
The child wrote the required entrypoint and libraries, and artifact validation found the assembled deliverable files.
The delegated scope covered implementation, testing, and delivery; the adverse event was cancellation before completion, not an unowned pipeline.
The parent's initial probes informed delegation but were not a mandatory serial gate that alone blocked productive work.
There was no separate overlapping investigator phase followed by deferred implementation; the parent probed and then delegated one build.
No evidence shows workers concentrated on auxiliary work while a separate indispensable path lacked capacity; the direct event is child cancellation.
The parallel run used one child, not excessive breadth or repeated child fan-out that collectively exhausted budget.
The child scope was broad, but the same episode is more directly evidenced by explicit cancellation of an active child during needed verification.
The child brief included task requirements, ESM/no-dependency constraints, CLI behavior, validator behavior, and verification expectations.
There were no separately owned interoperating components from different children and no observed incompatible cross-agent interface.
No known parent finding is shown to disappear during transfer; the child received a detailed brief and acted on it.
The delegated prompt was large, but the child consumed it enough to implement modules and pass an initial differential harness.
No receiver consumed superseded workspace or requirement state; there was only one child implementation stream.
No incompatible reports or contracts reached the parent and remained unadjudicated before a decision.
The parent did not make an observable whole-task completion decision; the turn ended with cancellation and a failed child result.
No replacement or retry child was launched, so no retry repeated prior work without inherited checkpoints.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The delegated implementation child was active in an extended verification command when it was cancelled before a completed handoff, and the parent received a failed child result.
candidates.realized_consequence: The parent never received a completed child implementation and verification handoff, and extended verification remained unfinished at closure.
candidates.near_match_reason: The failed child result is downstream of the same cancellation, and the parent turn ended at that boundary without a distinct takeover opportunity.

candidates.reason: A deliverable was already present and artifact validation copied it; the missing step was not late promotion of an otherwise complete candidate.
No child result or implementation change was merged after integrated verification; the child wrote files before local verification.
The child did not complete a normal returned implementation handoff; its writes were already in /output, and the direct lifecycle event was cancellation.
The delegated child was not a separate verifier with a completed finding trapped below the parent; the child was stopped mid-verification.
The child failure and parent cancellation are the same terminal episode, so there is no separate observed period for takeover before closure.
No completed child result was available to the parent and ignored; the parent received a failed child result after cancellation.
Although the parent waited on the child, the retained direct boundary is explicit child cancellation during needed work, not a separate ignored-progress episode.
Only one child wrote the implementation files, and no competing cross-file design from another live agent required reconciliation.
There is no observed event where two live agents edited the same source or configuration file.
No non-entry library or configuration source produced by another agent was replaced or rewritten by a different live owner.
No required entrypoint or submitted artifact was replaced while another agent owned or used that deliverable.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple current outputs or invalidated another agent's final-tree work.
The child wrote in the shared /output workspace, but no concrete unstable-state or provenance problem from multiple live writers is evidenced.
No generated cache, fixture, temporary path, tool, process, or auxiliary implementation from one actor was consumed by another as stable input.
